messages:
jia: Quick async ask — need a perf + quality compare for customer-omega workload. Target compares int4 vs FP8 on our rtx-pool. Key constraints: avg request ~80 tokens, some long tails, KV-cache warm/unwarm. Can someone kick off benchmarks (batch 1/4/8) and run qeval-regression (promptset-regress-91) and post p50/p95/p99 + quality delta? Also pinging for a quick gating recommendation (rollback threshold). PR with minor runtime hooks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/412

sam: I can run this now. Which dataset exactly and any seed we should use?

jia: Use prod-tailset-v2, seed=42. Include both cold start (uncached) and warm (KV primed) runs. Please capture cost-per-token estimate and throughput too.

miguel: I'll run the qeval suite against the two quant configs and report EM/ppl/token-lev metrics. FYI promptset-regress-91 includes the customer edge prompts we saw last week.

bench-bot: Started job "perf-run-1967354321" on rtx-pool (nodes=6). Config: --quant=int4,fp8 --batch=1,4,8 --dataset=prod-tailset-v2 --seed=42. ETA ~7m.

sam: Results (top-line). All runs on rtx-pool, sequence cap 512. Uncached/cold first token latency, then streaming token latencies.

```
Config   p50(ms)  p95(ms)  p99(ms)  throughput(tok/s)  cost_est($/1M tok)
int4     84       185      420      32                0.023
fp8      92       210      465      28                0.031
```

Quality (quick qeval): int4 vs fp8 on promptset-regress-91 (higher is better except ppl)

```
Metric    fp8    int4   delta
EM        0.784  0.768  -0.016 (-1.6%)
PPL       12.1   12.8   +0.7
BLEU      34.2   33.6   -0.6
```

Notes: int4 shows clear perf/cost wins, p99 improved ~10% in absolute ms, but EM drop ~1.6% (stat sig on bootstrap ~p=0.03).

anya: Nice, thanks. Do you have latency breakdown for long-tail (>512 tokens) requests or attention blowup cases? We care about p99.9 for the customer.

sam: I ran a long-tail subset (n=120 long requests). p99.9 numbers are noisy but trend similar: int4 p99.9 ~1.2s, fp8 ~1.35s. Variance higher on int4 for sequences with many KV flushes — probably kernel-level mem-layout degenerate cases.

kevin: For rollout gating, propose: block if EM delta <= -2.0% OR p99 increased by >15% vs baseline. Given numbers, int4 is within p99 gate but EM is borderline. Suggest canary at 5% traffic with close eval hooks and auto-rollback if EM drops >1.8% on live promptset.

jia: Agree with kevin. Also add a manual approval for any customer-facing rollout >10%. I'll set up canary config: A/B 50/50 within canary traffic slice? Actually we want control: 5% users -> 50/50 int4/fp8 inside that group, collect metrics for 24h, if EM diff <= -1.8% AND p99 <= +10% then expand.

miguel: I'll add the qeval check to the PR (#412) and wire the canary alert for EM regression and p99 tail. @sam @anya can you review the PR? It adds a small scoring hook and a CI job that runs promptset-regress-91 as part of canary validation.

sam: Reviewing now, left small comment about the perf-flag parsing.

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: 5% traffic -> split(50/50) start 1967355000 (in ~12m). Auto-check window 24h.

jia: Thanks all — this gives us a clear path. If CI + canary metrics look good we'll flip default to int4 for this customer. Filing follow-up doc in #eng-runtime-ops later. Closing thread. :thumbsup:
